name: Authority as allowlist instead of closed-schema positive proof
invariant: A conclusion may be drawn only from ONE atomic pass that positively proves conformance to a single declared, closed schema; authority defaults to none and is NEVER inferred from the absence of a failing check.
cues: the validator is a growing ladder of per-property die()/if checks discovered one adversary at a time
'validated' means 'the substrings/fields I remembered to check passed', not 'the whole document conforms'
each QA round finds a NEW corruption/drift shape the previous round did not enumerate (r1->r2->r3 same spine)
additionalProperties is open in effect: an admitted-key-set is treated as a closed schema
the brief/finding says 'add a check for X' rather than 'prove conformance to the schema'
fix: Replace the enumerated per-property check ladder with conformance to one committed closed schema (additionalProperties:false, full required, exact type, enum, uniqueItems) proven in a single pass; any property the schema does not positively admit is a failure. Prove conformance; do not spot-check known-bad shapes.

provenance.note: authority defined as a growing ad-hoc conjunction of checks rather than one positive invariant with a fail-closed default
authority = enumerated conjunction of hand-authored per-property predicates instead of conformance to one closed schema
type validation keeps false-passing across three implementations (uphold FAIL)
partial-ID audit deemed globally authoritative under a reactively-assembled validator

name: Absence read as discharge
invariant: An obligation is cleared ONLY by positive proof from a fresh, structurally-complete, authoritative snapshot that provably enumerates that obligation's status; absent/stale/corrupt/partial coverage RETAINS the prior fact unchanged (fail-open when CREATING a block, fail-closed when DISCHARGING one).
cues: code concludes 'id absent from the current set => accounted/done/discharged'
a stale or partially-read file is allowed to shrink or clear a tracked set
a 'count == length' style check is treated as proof of complete coverage
a timeout/contention path silently drops the occurrence it could not record
fix: Consume coverage as positive per-item proof; retain every prior obligation whenever the source is non-authoritative for any reason; never read an id's absence-from-a-set-of-unknown-coverage as accounted; keep block creation fail-open and block discharge fail-closed by construction.

provenance.note: the gate decides an order's fate by inference from the audit file's silence; absence read as discharge
non-authoritative audit covers no id; every prior order:X is retained
stale read reporting zero orders dropped a prior blocked order (silence was discharge)
contention timeout must not silently discard the occurrence; preserve an append-safe fallback record

name: Digest/verification not covering the whole document
invariant: A content digest or verification that gates a mutation must hash the ENTIRE canonical document (minus only explicitly-excluded volatile keys), so a change to ANY field - including fields no check enumerates - invalidates the approval.
cues: the approval digest/hash is computed over a hand-selected subset of fields
the parser scrapes first-occurrence substrings (regex/jq -e .) instead of parsing the whole document
a mutation to an un-enumerated field still passes an 'approved' gate
a per-field comparison enumerates 'the fields we check' rather than proving whole-object equality
fix: Compute the digest over the whole canonical serialization (sorted keys; exclude only named volatile keys) and recompute-and-compare before any mutation; parse whole documents with a strict loader instead of grepping first-occurrence substrings; compare the whole replayed object, not a hand-picked set of leaves.

provenance.note: r1 scraped substrings; validated meant the substrings I grepped for were present
computeDigest now hashes the canonical WHOLE proposal document rather than a hand-selected projection (migrate.mjs:95-116)
manifest digest recomputed and the whole replayed object (counts/omitted/fallbackReason/identity) compared, not selected leaves

name: Fail-open on a missing prerequisite tool
invariant: When a required validation engine/tool is absent, the validator REFUSES (stable code, non-zero exit) - never a best-effort, warn-and-pass, or weaker path. There is no code path in which a missing tool yields success.
cues: command -v X || <skip the check> / <weaker path>
'if python3/jq/jsonschema/timeout absent, fall back to ...'
a duplicate/type/deadline check that only runs when an optional tool is present
the fix relies on GNU-only tooling that is simply absent on a supported platform (macOS)
fix: Make every engine a HARD prerequisite that prints a stable *_UNAVAILABLE code and exits non-zero when missing; test each absent-tool path explicitly and independently; never gate a correctness check on the presence of an optional dependency.

provenance.note: python3+PyYAML+jsonschema are hard prerequisites; if any is absent print PROFILE_VALIDATOR_UNAVAILABLE and exit 1, never warn-and-pass
MUST NOT degrade when any engine is absent
engine fail-closed / no-degradation contract under absent tool

name: Proof/validation not atomic with the mutation it authorizes
invariant: The values a mutation is authorized against must come from the SAME atomic read/parse that validated them, and the proof (or audit annotation) must be atomic with the mutation, so no consumer can ever observe a different generation than the one validated.
cues: two jq/parse passes over the same file (validate, then re-read the ids/values)
a proof written non-atomically with the mutation it attests
a per-row audit annotation that is not atomic with the reconciliation it records
a pair of writes/renames each individually atomic but not jointly atomic or writer-serialized
fix: One parse per artifact feeds duplicate-rejection, validation, and the downstream consume, emitting the validated payload from the validating pass; make the proof/annotation atomic with (or transactionally bound to) the mutation; close the two-pass read race.

provenance.note: one atomic jq pass validates AND emits the ids so no consumer sees a different generation (MUST NOT read in two passes)
F3 - proof mutation and proof verification are not atomic/complete
the required per-row audit annotation is not atomic with reconciliation
each rename is atomic but the pair is not atomic or writer-serialized

name: Unbounded/synchronous wait on a critical path
invariant: Any call on a latency-critical path (spawn, dispatch, turn-end) must be bounded by a PORTABLE hard deadline that a missing tool cannot defeat, and must fail-open to the no-op outcome when the deadline hits - never block the critical operation.
cues: a helper invoked synchronously on the spawn/dispatch path with no timeout
|| true that handles a non-zero exit but NOT a child that never returns
a deadline implemented with a GNU-only timeout that is absent on a supported host
a network/HTTP/recall call awaited inline on the critical path
fix: Wrap the call in a portable deadline (a PID-watchdog fallback when GNU timeout/gtimeout are absent) that kills only the exact recorded child PID and returns the fail-open outcome; regression-test the no-timeout PATH; keep recall/delivery out-of-band so it can never wedge the primary.

provenance.note: injection cannot block a spawn - FAIL: the memory CLI is executed synchronously with no timeout (fm-memory-inject.sh:113)
supported hosts without GNU timeout remain unbounded
fix - portable PID-watchdog deadline completes a 2s budget against a 12s child, brief unchanged
delivery must never touch the composer/transcript path and must never block a spawn

name: Stale artifact preserved on failure (cleanup-failure ignored)
invariant: On a failed or refused operation, any stale attestation/index/output must be provably invalidated (removed or atomically superseded) BEFORE proceeding, and a cleanup/unlink failure must itself fail the operation - never '|| true'. A stale artifact must never be read as a fresh, authoritative result.
cues: rm -f ... 2>/dev/null || true guarding an attestation/sidecar/lock
a stale derived index treated as a 'proven' result and consumed
an operation that leaves a partial/temp file on crash (no atomic rename)
'invalidate' that neither verifies the old artifact is gone nor refuses on failure
fix: Verify the stale artifact is actually gone (or atomically superseded) and refuse loudly if invalidation fails; write outputs via temp-file + fsync + atomic rename so a crash leaves no partial file; treat a stale/missing derived index as non-authoritative => no injection / no consume.

provenance.note: unlink refusal leaves stale authority; the unconditional || true neither verifies the old attestation is gone nor refuses
F1 - stale or missing derived index injects instead of failing open
fix pattern - temp write + fsync + atomic rename; the crashed child leaves no final partial file
